newsitem.title: USA: U.S. machine tool demand fell 16.5 pct in May.
newsitem.headline: U.S. machine tool demand fell 16.5 pct in May.

text.p: U.S. machine tool demand fell in May from the previous month, the American Machine Tool Distributors' Association and the Association for Manufacturing Technology said on Sunday in a joint report.
Total demand in May fell 16.5 percent to an estimated $678 million from a revised $811 million in April. But it rose 8.1 percent from the $627.3 million estimate a year earlier in May 1996.

"Plenty of steam remains in the engine, evident in the fact that only 15 percent of all machine tools in manufacturing facilities today are under five years of age," AMTDA President Ralph Nappi said in a statement.
"The productivity that new manufacturing technology provides is too tempting to ignore, especially considering the amount of capital available for reinvestment," Nappi added.
The April estimate was revised up from $801 million reported a month ago.
Orders in the first five months of 1997 were estimated at $3.47 billion, a 10.3 percent increase from the same period in 1996, the trade groups said.
Machine tools are used to shape metal in making everything from bicycles to aircraft. Demand for these tools can provide a leading indicator of the pace of manufacturing.

By region, the report said the Midwest accounted for 37.8 percent of national demand, followed by 19.3 percent in the Central region and 16.4 percent in the Northeast. The West accounted for 14.2 percent and the South 12.3 percent, it said.

"The Midwest experienced a needed breather in May machine tool orders, but compared to a year ago the national picture is still strong," Nappi said. The report said May Midwest orders fell about 36 percent from April and were also down about 10 percent from orders placed in the year-ago month.
Export orders placed with U.S. machine tool makers totaled 245 units in May, down from 263 units in April, the report said. Year-earlier export orders were not available.
Total export orders in the first five months of 1997 were 1,329 units, the report said.

The latest figures were from the 12th U.S. Machine Tool Consumption report, which replaced monthly data on U.S. machine tool orders, shipments and exports issued by the Association for Manufacturing Technology.
